ideas.title: Bogged: the yacht sinks into the beach you sail it onto
ideas.critique: Strong: this is the first idea in ten posts where the player causes the trouble and then fixes it with their hands and their friends, on ground that really deforms, and it gives the still yacht something it does. The risk is that digging and pushing turn into a canned 'unstick' animation over a sand patch that only exists around one cart, which would cap it as a one-case rig.

ideas.title: The beach remembers: every track until the tide takes it
ideas.critique: Persistent ground marks across the whole beach, which the tide and wind then erase, is something the island never had, and it quietly makes every creature's movement legible. As a goal, though, it is mostly something to look at: reading yesterday's tracks is charming once and gives the player little to do.

ideas.title: Plante's jar: a battery you form by charging it again and again
same_form: A top over a ring of lodestone
ideas.critique: It is another electrochemical device on a bench, watched while it fizzes, right after the clay pots; the plates browning cycle by cycle is an exact payoff but a slow one, and the eleventh physics study in a row. Its value is almost entirely on the road, not in what a viewer sees.

ideas.title: The windmill on the dune that the wind really turns
same_form: A top over a ring of lodestone
ideas.critique: A windmill turning a generator to light a wire is the most expected next step the big goal could produce, and it is filmed in the same form as the motor and the wire. Tuning the pitch against a changing solved wind is a real toy, but the pitch reads as the motor post played backwards.

ideas.title: The motor sings: its hum is its real current
ideas.critique: Sound driven straight by the simulated state is a channel the films hardly use, and driving by ear is a genuinely new way for the player to read the machine. But nobody drives the cart yet, so for now it is a hum on a bench motor.

ideas.title: Gears cut by hand for the dune
same_form: A top over a ring of lodestone
ideas.critique: Choosing two tooth counts on a bench is a road checkbox, with a pass/fail snap and nothing to see beyond teeth turning. There is no cart for the gears to lift up the dune, so the payoff it promises does not exist yet.

ideas.title: Brake down the far side, charge it back
ideas.critique: It needs the cart, the accumulator and the motor-dynamo all working first, so made now it would be a staged descent with a fizz written on top. The idea itself, a lock-up and slide in real sand, is a good one when its parts exist.

ideas.title: Tug of war on the beach
ideas.critique: It is a creature-with-creature game people would play and show, and where the feet stand decides who wins, which is a nice rule. The risk is that a rope plus a traction number gives a tug-meter with creatures leaning in poses, not bodies really digging and sliding.

ideas.title: Sail by the wool
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Telltales streaming in the sail's own solved flow make an invisible field readable and give trimming a real cue, and that is honest. It is a small, close-up detail on the yacht that is already listed on the road, so nobody who knows the island will be surprised.

ideas.title: A spark in the dark
ideas.critique: A glowing thing lighting what is near it at night has been done with the hot glass, and an arc drawn as an emissive light at each segment break is mostly a look. It previews the big goal's moment without the cart, the friends or the dusk that make that moment.
